title: CTS The Doctrine of the Church — Unit 8

blocks.en: 📖 Systematic Theology — Unit 8: The Doctrine of the Church
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Teología Sistemática — Unidad 8: La Doctrina de la Iglesia

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "Christ loved the church and gave Himself for her." — Ephesians 5:25 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Cristo amó a la iglesia, y se entregó a sí mismo por ella." — Efesios 5:25 (RVG)

blocks.en: The Definition: People, Not Places
blocks.es_reference: La Definición: Personas, No Lugares

blocks.en: A few years ago, my wife and I went to Barcelona and we saw this magnificent church building, the Sagrada Família. It is perhaps the most breathtaking structure on earth — an architectural masterpiece of soaring spires and intricate stone. They have been working on the building for over 140 years, and it is still not completed. It stands as a monumental testament to human vision and persistence.
blocks.es_reference: Hace unos años, mi esposa y yo fuimos a Barcelona y vimos este magnífico edificio de iglesia, la Sagrada Família. Es quizás la estructura más impresionante de la tierra — una obra maestra arquitectónica de agujas elevadas y piedra intrincada. Han estado trabajando en el edificio por más de 140 años, y todavía no está terminado. Se erige como un testimonio monumental de la visión y persistencia humanas.

blocks.en: However, as amazing as the building is, it is not the Church.
blocks.es_reference: Sin embargo, por increíble que sea el edificio, no es la Iglesia.

blocks.en: The Church is not a physical location; it is a people. This is a fundamental distinction that much of the modern world has forgotten. We often speak of "going to church," but in the New Testament sense, you cannot go to a church; you can only gather as a church. For the first 250 years of its existence, the Church had no dedicated buildings whatsoever. There were no cathedrals, no steeples, and no designated "holy sites." Instead, believers met in homes, in the streets, and in hidden places.
blocks.es_reference: La Iglesia no es una ubicación física; es un pueblo. Esta es una distinción fundamental que gran parte del mundo moderno ha olvidado. A menudo hablamos de "ir a la iglesia", pero en el sentido del Nuevo Testamento, no se puede ir a una iglesia; solo se puede reunir como iglesia. Durante los primeros 250 años de su existencia, la Iglesia no tenía absolutamente ningún edificio dedicado. No había catedrales, ni campanarios, ni "sitios santos" designados. En cambio, los creyentes se reunían en casas, en las calles y en lugares escondidos.

blocks.en: During this "building-less" era, the growth of the Church was phenomenal. Without the overhead of physical facilities, the movement was agile and focused entirely on people. They understood that the Ekklesia was the "called-out assembly" of believers — the community itself — and not the mortar and stone where they gathered. If every cathedral on earth were leveled today, the Church of Jesus Christ would remain entirely intact because the Church is comprised of "Living Stones" (1 Peter 2:5). The structure is merely a shell; the life is in the assembly. We must never confuse the "chapel" with the "community." One is made of dead stone; the other is made of living souls redeemed by the blood of Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Durante esta era "sin edificios", el crecimiento de la Iglesia fue fenomenal. Sin la carga de las instalaciones físicas, el movimiento era ágil y enfocado completamente en las personas. Entendían que la Ekklesia era la "asamblea llamada" de creyentes — la comunidad misma — y no el mortero y la piedra donde se reunían. Si cada catedral en la tierra fuera arrasada hoy, la Iglesia de Jesucristo permanecería completamente intacta porque la Iglesia está compuesta de "Piedras Vivas" (1 Pedro 2:5). La estructura es meramente un cascarón; la vida está en la asamblea. Nunca debemos confundir la "capilla" con la "comunidad". Una está hecha de piedra muerta; la otra está hecha de almas vivas redimidas por la sangre de Cristo.

blocks.en: "You also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ." — 1 Peter 2:5
blocks.es_reference: "Vosotros también, como piedras vivas, sed edificados como casa espiritual y sacerdocio santo, para ofrecer sacrificios espirituales aceptables a Dios por medio de Jesucristo." — 1 Pedro 2:5

blocks.en: The Unified Office: One Role, Three Descriptions
blocks.es_reference: El Oficio Unificado: Un Rol, Tres Descripciones

blocks.en: When we examine the New Testament record regarding leadership, we find a consistent pattern. There were three specific Greek terms used to describe the leaders of the local assembly. While modern denominations have taken these three and separated them into different tiers of authority or different offices, the Biblical record suggests they all likely described the same office and function.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando examinamos el registro del Nuevo Testamento sobre el liderazgo, encontramos un patrón consistente. Había tres términos griegos específicos utilizados para describir a los líderes de la asamblea local. Mientras que las denominaciones modernas han tomado estos tres y los han separado en diferentes niveles de autoridad o diferentes oficios, el registro bíblico sugiere que todos probablemente describían el mismo oficio y función.

blocks.en: Episkopos (Bishop/Overseer): This term emphasizes the function of management, organization, and oversight. It points to the responsibility of the office.
blocks.es_reference: Episkopos (Obispo/Supervisor): Este término enfatiza la función de gestión, organización y supervisión. Apunta a la responsabilidad del oficio.

blocks.en: Presbuteros (Elder): This term emphasizes the character, maturity, and wisdom of the leader. It points to the dignity of the office.
blocks.es_reference: Presbuteros (Anciano): Este término enfatiza el carácter, la madurez y la sabiduría del líder. Apunta a la dignidad del oficio.

blocks.en: Poimen (Pastor/Shepherd): This term emphasizes the duty of feeding, caring for, and protecting the flock. It points to the heart of the office.
blocks.es_reference: Poimen (Pastor): Este término enfatiza el deber de alimentar, cuidar y proteger al rebaño. Apunta al corazón del oficio.

blocks.en: In the early church, these were not three different jobs; they were three ways of describing the same man doing God's work. A leader was an elder in his maturity, a bishop in his oversight, and a pastor in his heart for the sheep.
blocks.es_reference: En la iglesia primitiva, estos no eran tres trabajos diferentes; eran tres maneras de describir al mismo hombre haciendo la obra de Dios. Un líder era un anciano en su madurez, un obispo en su supervisión y un pastor en su corazón por las ovejas.

blocks.en: "Therefore take heed to yourselves and to all the flock, among which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers (episkopos), to shepherd (poimen) the church of God." — Acts 20:28
blocks.es_reference: "Por tanto, mirad por vosotros, y por todo el rebaño en que el Espíritu Santo os ha puesto por obispos, para apacentar la iglesia del Señor." — Hechos 20:28

blocks.en: The Ordinances: The Enacted Gospel
blocks.es_reference: Las Ordenanzas: El Evangelio Actuado

blocks.en: A true church is identified by the faithful preaching of the Word and the proper administration of the Ordinances. We must view Baptism and the Lord's Supper as more than mere symbols or rituals; they are the Gospel enacted in physical form.
blocks.es_reference: Una iglesia verdadera se identifica por la predicación fiel de la Palabra y la administración adecuada de las Ordenanzas. Debemos ver el Bautismo y la Cena del Señor como más que meros símbolos o rituales; son el Evangelio actuado en forma física.

blocks.en: 1. Baptism (The Gospel of Identity): In baptism, the Gospel is physically performed. As the believer is placed under the water and raised back up, they are enacting the death, burial, and resurrection of Christ. It is the outward drama of an inward change — a public identification with the work of Jesus. It does not save, but it testifies that salvation has already occurred.
blocks.es_reference: 1. Bautismo (El Evangelio de la Identidad): En el bautismo, el Evangelio se realiza físicamente. A medida que el creyente es puesto bajo el agua y levantado nuevamente, está actuando la muerte, sepultura y resurrección de Cristo. Es el drama externo de un cambio interno — una identificación pública con la obra de Jesús. No salva, pero testifica que la salvación ya ha ocurrido.

blocks.en: "Therefore we were buried with Him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life." — Romans 6:4
blocks.es_reference: "Porque somos sepultados juntamente con él para muerte por el bautismo, a fin de que como Cristo resucitó de los muertos por la gloria del Padre, así también nosotros andemos en vida nueva." — Romanos 6:4

blocks.en: 2. The Lord's Supper (The Gospel of Remembrance): When the church gathers for the bread and the cup, they are enacting the sacrifice of Calvary. By eating and drinking together, the assembly is participating in a physical sermon that "proclaims the Lord's death until He comes." It is the Gospel made visible through the shared elements of the table. It is also a time of reflection. Believers are called to examine themselves, remembering the seriousness of sin and the greatness of Christ's sacrifice.
blocks.es_reference: 2. La Cena del Señor (El Evangelio del Recuerdo): Cuando la iglesia se reúne para el pan y la copa, están actuando el sacrificio del Calvario. Al comer y beber juntos, la asamblea está participando en un sermón físico que "anuncia la muerte del Señor hasta que él venga". Es el Evangelio hecho visible a través de los elementos compartidos de la mesa. También es un tiempo de reflexión. Se llama a los creyentes a examinarse a sí mismos, recordando la seriedad del pecado y la grandeza del sacrificio de Cristo.

blocks.en: "For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death till He comes." — 1 Corinthians 11:26
blocks.es_reference: "Así, pues, todas las veces que comiereis este pan, y bebiereis esta copa, la muerte del Señor anunciáis hasta que él venga." — 1 Corintios 11:26

blocks.en: 💡 The Sagrada Família: A breathtaking cathedral in Barcelona, under construction for over 140 years. As amazing as the building is, it is not the Church. The Church is not a physical location; it is a people. For the first 250 years of Christianity, the church had no buildings — they met in homes and grew phenomenally. If every cathedral on earth were leveled today, the Church of Jesus Christ would remain entirely intact because the Church is comprised of living stones, not dead mortar.
blocks.es_reference: 💡 La Sagrada Família: Una catedral impresionante en Barcelona, en construcción por más de 140 años. Por increíble que sea el edificio, no es la Iglesia. La Iglesia no es una ubicación física; es un pueblo. Durante los primeros 250 años del cristianismo, la iglesia no tenía edificios — se reunían en casas y crecían fenomenalmente. Si cada catedral en la tierra fuera arrasada hoy, la Iglesia de Jesucristo permanecería completamente intacta porque la Iglesia está compuesta de piedras vivas, no de mortero muerto.

blocks.en: The Three-Fold Mission
blocks.es_reference: La Misión Triple

blocks.en: The Church is a community with a specific, three-dimensional movement. It functions as the "Body" of Christ in the world through three distinct directions:
blocks.es_reference: La Iglesia es una comunidad con un movimiento específico y tridimensional. Funciona como el "Cuerpo" de Cristo en el mundo a través de tres direcciones distintas:

blocks.en: Upward (Worship): The Church looks up to acknowledge the supremacy and holiness of God. This is our primary purpose — to glorify the Creator through praise and the proclamation of His truth. Worship is not limited to a service, but it finds a special expression when the church gathers together.
blocks.es_reference: Hacia Arriba (Adoración): La Iglesia mira hacia arriba para reconocer la supremacía y santidad de Dios. Este es nuestro propósito primario — glorificar al Creador a través de la alabanza y la proclamación de Su verdad. La adoración no está limitada a un servicio, pero encuentra una expresión especial cuando la iglesia se reúne.

blocks.en: Inward (Edification): The Church looks at itself for the purpose of mutual growth. This is the work of Koinonia (fellowship), involving teaching and encouraging one another so that the "Living Stones" are properly shaped and fitted together. Believers are called to share life together, encouraging one another, bearing burdens, and building one another up.
blocks.es_reference: Hacia Adentro (Edificación): La Iglesia se mira a sí misma con el propósito del crecimiento mutuo. Este es el trabajo de Koinonía (comunión), involucrando enseñar y animarse unos a otros para que las "Piedras Vivas" sean apropiadamente formadas y ensambladas. Se llama a los creyentes a compartir la vida juntos, animándose unos a otros, llevando cargas y edificándose unos a otros.

blocks.en: Outward (Evangelism): The Church looks at the world. This is the movement of the Scarlet Thread. Having been reconciled to God, the Church carries the message and invitation of that reconciliation to those who are still outside the assembly. It is called to proclaim the gospel and to make disciples. This mission extends beyond the walls of the church into the world.
blocks.es_reference: Hacia Afuera (Evangelismo): La Iglesia mira al mundo. Este es el movimiento del Hilo Escarlata. Habiendo sido reconciliada con Dios, la Iglesia lleva el mensaje y la invitación de esa reconciliación a aquellos que todavía están fuera de la asamblea. Es llamada a proclamar el evangelio y a hacer discípulos. Esta misión se extiende más allá de las paredes de la iglesia hacia el mundo.

blocks.en: "Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit." — Matthew 28:19
blocks.es_reference: "Por tanto, id, y enseñad a todas las naciones, bautizándoles en el nombre del Padre, y del Hijo, y del Espíritu Santo." (es decir, haced discípulos) — Mateo 28:19

blocks.en: The Body of Christ: Many Members, One Purpose
blocks.es_reference: El Cuerpo de Cristo: Muchos Miembros, Un Propósito

blocks.en: The Apostle Paul uses the metaphor of the human body to describe the church. A body has many parts — eyes, ears, hands, feet — and each part has a different function. None is greater, and none is lesser. The eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you." In the same way, every believer has a role to play. No one is unnecessary, and no one is sufficient alone.
blocks.es_reference: El apóstol Pablo usa la metáfora del cuerpo humano para describir la iglesia. Un cuerpo tiene muchas partes — ojos, oídos, manos, pies — y cada parte tiene una función diferente. Ninguna es mayor, y ninguna es menor. El ojo no puede decir a la mano: "No tengo necesidad de ti." Del mismo modo, cada creyente tiene un papel que desempeñar. Nadie es innecesario, y nadie es suficiente solo.

blocks.en: The Eye of Vision: In a physical body, the eyes don't create the path; they simply perceive the path that is already there. As Henry Blackaby taught, spiritual vision isn't about us coming up with a clever plan and asking God to bless it. It is about looking for where God is already at work and simply joining Him. It is the difference between asking, "What can we do for God?" and asking, "What is God doing that He wants us to be part of?"
blocks.es_reference: El Ojo de la Visión: En un cuerpo físico, los ojos no crean el camino; simplemente perciben el camino que ya está allí. Como enseñó Henry Blackaby, la visión espiritual no se trata de que se nos ocurra un plan ingenioso y le pidamos a Dios que lo bendiga. Se trata de buscar dónde Dios ya está obrando y simplemente unirnos a Él. Es la diferencia entre preguntar: "¿Qué podemos hacer por Dios?" y preguntar: "¿Qué está haciendo Dios de lo que Él quiere que seamos parte?"

blocks.en: The Ear of Compassion: The church is the body that listens when the world turns a deaf ear. We stop to hear a soul. We ask about people's lives. We become members of the Body who listen.
blocks.es_reference: El Oído de la Compasión: La iglesia es el cuerpo que escucha cuando el mundo hace oídos sordos. Nos detenemos para escuchar a un alma. Preguntamos sobre las vidas de las personas. Nos convertimos en miembros del Cuerpo que escuchan.

blocks.en: The Foot of Evangelism: "How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!" (Romans 10:15). Those "beautiful feet" are not our own — they are God's grace moving through people who are willing to take the step. The glory belongs to the One who waits for us to finally take the step.
blocks.es_reference: El Pie del Evangelismo: "¡Cuán hermosos son los pies de los que anuncian buenas nuevas!" (Romanos 10:15). Esos "hermosos pies" no son los nuestros — son la gracia de Dios moviéndose a través de personas que están dispuestas a dar el paso. La gloria pertenece a Aquel que espera que finalmente demos el paso.

blocks.en: "For as the body is one and has many members, but all the members of that one body, being many, are one body, so also is Christ." — 1 Corinthians 12:12
blocks.es_reference: "Porque así como el cuerpo es uno, y tiene muchos miembros, pero todos los miembros del cuerpo, siendo muchos, son un solo cuerpo, así también Cristo." — 1 Corintios 12:12

blocks.en: The Church is Loved
blocks.es_reference: La Iglesia es Amada

blocks.en: The Church is Loved: Ephesians 5:25 says, "Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her." The Greek term for love used here is agape, signifying a selfless, sacrificial, and volitional commitment. The Church is not merely a human organization or a social club; it is the specific object of Christ's divine affection. Christ didn't just love the idea of a church; He loved the people who compose it enough to endure the cross. We should never criticize the Bride of Christ. If Christ, who is perfect, loved the Church enough to die for it, then we, as His followers, cannot claim to love the Head (Christ) while despising or neglecting the Body (the Church).
blocks.es_reference: La Iglesia es Amada: Efesios 5:25 dice: "Maridos, amad a vuestras mujeres, así como Cristo amó a la iglesia, y se entregó a sí mismo por ella." El término griego para amor usado aquí es ágape, que significa un compromiso desinteresado, sacrificial y volitivo. La Iglesia no es meramente una organización humana o un club social; es el objeto específico del afecto divino de Cristo. Cristo no solo amó la idea de una iglesia; amó a las personas que la componen lo suficiente como para soportar la cruz. Nunca debemos criticar a la Esposa de Cristo. Si Cristo, quien es perfecto, amó a la Iglesia lo suficiente como para morir por ella, entonces nosotros, como Sus seguidores, no podemos afirmar amar a la Cabeza (Cristo) mientras despreciamos o descuidamos al Cuerpo (la Iglesia).

blocks.en: The Church is Holy and Called
blocks.es_reference: La Iglesia es Santa y Llamada

blocks.en: The Church is Holy: The command for this "unblemished" church is found in 1 Peter 1:15-16: "But as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation; Because it is written, Be ye holy; for I am holy." To be a holy church means we are a people who have been set apart by the Spirit for God's exclusive use. In the Old Testament Temple, access to the Holy of Holies was restricted. When Jesus died, the veil was split from top to bottom (Matthew 27:51). This was God's way of saying the door is open. But holiness is what keeps the power flowing. We are the Holy Church. We are designed to carry the power of God to a world in need. To be holy is to maintain the "Clean Room" of our fellowship so that God's power can flow through us to the world without interference.
blocks.es_reference: La Iglesia es Santa: El mandato para esta iglesia "sin mancha" se encuentra en 1 Pedro 1:15-16: "Sino, como aquel que os llamó es santo, sed también vosotros santos en toda vuestra manera de vivir; porque escrito está: Sed santos, porque yo soy santo." Ser una iglesia santa significa que somos un pueblo que ha sido apartado por el Espíritu para el uso exclusivo de Dios. En el Templo del Antiguo Testamento, el acceso al Lugar Santísimo estaba restringido. Cuando Jesús murió, el velo se rasgó de arriba abajo (Mateo 27:51). Esta era la manera de Dios de decir que la puerta está abierta. Pero la santidad es lo que mantiene fluyendo el poder. Somos la Iglesia Santa. Estamos diseñados para llevar el poder de Dios a un mundo necesitado. Ser santo es mantener el "Cuarto Limpio" de nuestra comunión para que el poder de Dios pueda fluir a través de nosotros al mundo sin interferencia.

blocks.en: "But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, His own special people, that you may proclaim the praises of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light." — 1 Peter 2:9
blocks.es_reference: "Mas vosotros sois linaje escogido, real sacerdocio, nación santa, pueblo adquirido por Dios, para que anunciéis las virtudes de aquel que os llamó de las tinieblas a su luz admirable." — 1 Pedro 2:9

blocks.en: Final Summary
blocks.es_reference: Resumen Final

blocks.en: The Doctrine of the Church teaches us that the Church is not a building but a people — the called-out assembly of believers. It is the body of Christ, the bride of Christ, and the household of God. Its leaders are described as elders, bishops, and pastors — one office with three descriptions. Its ordinances are baptism and the Lord's Supper — the gospel enacted. Its mission is threefold: upward (worship), inward (edification), and outward (evangelism). The Church is loved by Christ, called to be holy, and empowered by the Spirit. To neglect the Church is to neglect a central part of God's design. To love the Church is to love what Christ loves. To serve the Church is to serve the body of which He is the head.
blocks.es_reference: La Doctrina de la Iglesia nos enseña que la Iglesia no es un edificio sino un pueblo — la asamblea llamada de creyentes. Es el cuerpo de Cristo, la esposa de Cristo y la familia de Dios. Sus líderes son descritos como ancianos, obispos y pastores — un oficio con tres descripciones. Sus ordenanzas son el bautismo y la Cena del Señor — el evangelio actuado. Su misión es triple: hacia arriba (adoración), hacia adentro (edificación) y hacia afuera (evangelismo). La Iglesia es amada por Cristo, llamada a ser santa y empoderada por el Espíritu. Descuidar la Iglesia es descuidar una parte central del diseño de Dios. Amar la Iglesia es amar lo que Cristo ama. Servir a la Iglesia es servir al cuerpo del cual Él es la cabeza.

blocks.en: "And He put all things under His feet, and gave Him to be head over all things to the church, which is His body, the fullness of Him who fills all in all." — Ephesians 1:22-23
blocks.es_reference: "Y sometió todas las cosas bajo sus pies, y lo dio por cabeza sobre todas las cosas a la iglesia, la cual es su cuerpo, la plenitud de Aquel que todo lo llena en todo." — Efesios 1:22-23

mc.stem: The church is best understood as:
options: A people called out by God
mc.why: The church is a people — the called-out assembly of believers.

mc.stem: The word 'church' (ekklesia) refers to:
mc.why: Ekklesia means 'called-out ones' — the people God claims.

mc.stem: For how long did the early church have no dedicated buildings?
mc.why: For the first 250 years, the church had no buildings; they met in homes.

mc.stem: The three Greek terms for church leaders (episkopos, presbuteros, poimen) likely describe:
options: Three different offices with different authority
The same office and function from different angles
mc.why: These three terms describe the same office — elder (character), bishop (function), pastor (duty).

mc.stem: What does 'episkopos' emphasize?
mc.why: Episkopos (bishop/overseer) emphasizes the function of management and oversight.

mc.stem: What does 'presbuteros' emphasize?
mc.why: Presbuteros (elder) emphasizes the character, maturity, and wisdom of the leader.

mc.stem: What does 'poimen' emphasize?
options: Feeding, caring for, and protecting the flock
mc.why: Poimen (pastor/shepherd) emphasizes the duty of feeding, caring for, and protecting the flock.

mc.stem: The two ordinances of the church are:
mc.why: The two ordinances are Baptism and the Lord's Supper — the gospel enacted.

mc.stem: Baptism represents:
options: Identification with Christ's death, burial, and resurrection
mc.why: Baptism enacts the death, burial, and resurrection of Christ.

mc.stem: The Lord's Supper is a:
mc.why: The Lord's Supper is a remembrance of Christ's sacrifice.

mc.stem: The three-fold mission of the church is:
mc.why: The three-fold mission is upward (worship), inward (edification), and outward (evangelism).

mc.stem: The Greek word 'Koinonia' refers to:
mc.why: Koinonia refers to deep fellowship, sharing life together.

mc.stem: The church is called the 'Body of Christ' to emphasize:
options: Many members with different functions working together
mc.why: The body metaphor emphasizes unity in diversity — many parts, one purpose.

mc.stem: The church is called the 'Bride of Christ' to emphasize:
mc.why: The bride metaphor emphasizes devotion, love, and faithful relationship.

mc.stem: The church is called the 'Household of God' to emphasize:
mc.why: The household metaphor emphasizes family relationship and belonging.

mc.stem: According to 1 Peter 2:5, believers are described as:
mc.why: Believers are 'living stones' being built into a spiritual house.

mc.stem: Who is the only authorized 'Head' of the Church?
mc.why: Jesus Christ is the head of the church, His body (Ephesians 1:22-23).

mc.stem: The church is called to be 'holy' which means:
options: Set apart by God for His exclusive use
mc.why: Holiness means being set apart by God for His exclusive use and purpose.

mc.stem: What does the Sagrada Família illustration teach about the church?
options: The church is a people, not a building
Barcelona is the center of Christianity
mc.why: The Sagrada Família is a magnificent building, but it is not the church. The church is the people.

mc.stem: The purpose of spiritual gifts in the church is:
options: Building up the body of Christ
mc.why: Spiritual gifts are given for the edification and building up of the church.

The Greek term ____ (bishop or overseer) emphasizes the function of management, organization, and oversight.
The Greek term Presbuteros, meaning ____, emphasizes the character, maturity, and wisdom of the leader.
The lesson calls the ordinances "the ____ Gospel": in Baptism and the Lord's Supper the gospel is acted out in physical form.
As the believer is placed under the water and raised back up, baptism enacts the death, ____, and resurrection of Christ.
"For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's ____ till He comes." (1 Corinthians 11:26)
The inward mission of the Church, edification, is the work of ____, which means fellowship.

sa.prompt: Explain the distinction between the church as a building and the church as a people. Why is this distinction important for understanding the New Testament?
sa.model: The unit insists that in the New Testament the church is people, not a place. The word for church refers to a called-out assembly of believers, not to a structure of stone and wood. This distinction matters because if we confuse the church with a building, we misread the whole New Testament, which never treats the church as real estate but as the community of those redeemed by Christ. The early Christians had no special buildings, yet they were fully the church wherever they gathered. Understanding the church as people keeps the focus on the living body of believers, their fellowship, mission, and holiness, rather than on architecture, and it reminds us that the church exists even where there is no building at all.

sa.prompt: Explain the relationship between the three Greek terms for church leadership: episkopos, presbuteros, and poimen. How do they describe the same office?
sa.model: The unit teaches that three Greek terms describe one and the same office of leadership from different angles. Episkopos means overseer or bishop and stresses the work of watching over and superintending the flock. Presbuteros means elder and stresses the maturity, wisdom, and dignity of the one who leads. Poimen means shepherd or pastor and stresses the work of feeding, guiding, and caring for the sheep. These are not three ranks stacked on top of one another but three descriptions of a single role, since the New Testament uses them interchangeably for the same leaders. Together they teach that the one who leads the church oversees with care, leads with mature wisdom, and shepherds the people, so the office is best understood by holding all three pictures together.

sa.prompt: Explain the meaning of baptism and the Lord's Supper as "the Gospel enacted." What does each ordinance communicate about the work of Christ?
sa.model: The unit calls the ordinances the gospel enacted, meaning they dramatize in visible form what the gospel proclaims in words. Baptism pictures the believer's union with Christ in His death, burial, and resurrection: going down into the water shows death and burial to the old life, and rising from it shows new life in Christ. The Lord's Supper pictures the cost of that salvation: the broken bread speaks of Christ's body given and the cup of His blood shed for the forgiveness of sins. Each ordinance therefore preaches the work of Christ without words, baptism marking entrance into new life and the Supper repeatedly recalling the sacrifice that purchased it. They do not save by themselves, but they enact and proclaim the gospel they point to.

sa.prompt: Describe the threefold mission of the church: upward, inward, and outward. Why are all three necessary for a healthy church?
sa.model: The unit describes the church's mission as moving in three directions. The upward dimension is worship: the church exists first to glorify and adore God. The inward dimension is fellowship and edification: believers build one another up, care for one another, and grow together in maturity. The outward dimension is evangelism and mission: the church carries the gospel to the world. All three are necessary because neglecting any one produces an unhealthy church. A church that only looks up may become detached; one that only looks inward becomes ingrown and self-absorbed; one that only looks outward burns out and loses its depth. A healthy church keeps the three in balance, worshiping God, building up its members, and reaching the lost, because each dimension feeds and corrects the others.

sa.prompt: Using the body metaphor (1 Corinthians 12), explain why every member of the church is necessary. What happens when some members do not function?
sa.model: Paul compares the church to a body with many members, and the unit draws out why each one matters. Just as a body needs eyes, hands, and feet doing their different work, the church needs every member exercising his particular gift; no one is dispensable and no one can say he is not needed. The members are interdependent: each supplies something the others lack, so the whole functions only when each part does its work. When some members fail to function, the body is impaired, like a body missing the use of a limb; gifts go unused, burdens fall unevenly on others, and the church does not become what it should. The metaphor teaches both humility, since no member is the whole body, and responsibility, since when one part suffers or sits idle the whole body is affected.

sa.prompt: What does it mean that the church is "holy," and what does the "Clean Room" illustration teach about why holiness matters for the church's effectiveness?
sa.model: For the church to be holy means it is set apart for God, distinct from the world in purity and purpose. The unit uses the clean room to teach why this matters for effectiveness. A clean room, such as one used for delicate manufacturing or medical work, must be kept free of contamination, because even small impurities ruin the work done there; its usefulness depends on its purity. In the same way, the church's effectiveness depends on its holiness: when it lets the contamination of sin and worldliness in, it loses its power to do the work God intends. The illustration teaches that holiness is not optional fussiness but the very condition of usefulness; a contaminated church cannot accomplish its purpose, just as a contaminated clean room cannot do its job.

sa.prompt: Why should believers "never criticize the Bride of Christ"? What does this reveal about Christ's love for the church?
sa.model: The unit calls the church the Bride of Christ and warns believers against criticizing her, because of what that title reveals about Christ's love. A husband who deeply loves his bride does not take kindly to her being despised, and Christ loves the church as His own bride, having given Himself for her. To attack and tear down the church is therefore to speak against someone Christ cherishes and gave His life to win. This does not mean the church has no faults or that real problems should be ignored; it means our posture toward her should be the loving, building-up attitude of someone who honors what Christ loves, not the contempt of an outside critic. Understanding the church as the beloved Bride reframes how we speak of her: she is imperfect yet dearly loved by her Lord.

sa.prompt: What do the images of the "eye of vision," the "ear of compassion," and the "foot of evangelism" teach about how believers serve in the body of Christ?
sa.model: Extending the body metaphor, the unit uses three pictures to teach how believers serve. The eye of vision represents those who perceive needs, opportunities, and direction, helping the body see where to go. The ear of compassion represents those who listen to and feel the hurts of others, so the body hears the cries around it. The foot of evangelism represents those who go and carry the gospel out into the world. These images teach that the body needs different functions working together: seeing, hearing, and going are all required, and no single role is the whole. Believers serve by recognizing how they are gifted and playing their part, whether that is discerning direction, showing compassionate care, or actively reaching the lost, so that the whole body moves as one.

sa.prompt: What does it mean that the church is both "spiritual" and "visible"? How do these two aspects relate?
sa.model: The unit teaches that the church has two aspects held together. As spiritual, the church is the whole company of all true believers united to Christ, a reality not fully visible to human eyes since only God sees the heart. As visible, the church is the actual gathered community, the local congregation that meets, worships, and can be seen and joined. These relate as the inner reality and its outward expression: the spiritual church is made visible in real gatherings of believers, and the visible church is meant to embody the spiritual one. They are not two separate churches but two ways of seeing the one church. This guards against two errors: reducing the church to mere organization with no spiritual life, or treating it as so spiritual that the actual gathered congregation does not matter.

sa.prompt: Summarize the main point of Unit 8. Why is the doctrine of the church essential for Christian life and ministry?
sa.model: The main point of the unit is that the church is the people of God, not a building, the body of Christ in which every member has a function, led by shepherd-elders, marked out by baptism and the Lord's Supper, sent on a threefold mission of worship, fellowship, and evangelism, and called to be holy because it is loved by Christ as His Bride. The doctrine is essential for Christian life and ministry because no believer is meant to live the faith alone; we are members of one body, dependent on one another and accountable to one another. A right view of the church shapes how we worship, serve, use our gifts, and reach the world, and it guards us from both isolation and contempt for God's people. To love Christ is to love and serve His church.
